senses: Having some specific type of wrist.
One who speaks or writes in defense of a faith, a cause, or an institution.
Synonym of apologizer.
Resembling or characteristic of tomatoes.
examples: The sandwich toaster. It makes toasted sandwiches. Hot, buttery, cheesy, sardiney, tomatoey, anything-you-likey sandwiches.

senses: A mandatory, a sign or line that requires the path of the disc to be above, below or to one side of it.
The doctrine that a particular mental phenomenon, such as motivation or justification, has an internal rather than external basis
examples: In fleshing out the relations of perceptual justification and perceptual content attribution, both contenders thus grant epistemic internalism.

senses: The larva of any of the many moths of the family Noctuidae, considered an agricultural pest.
ety: From cut + worm, from the habit of eating through the stem of plants, or possibly from cutty (“short”).
examples: I listened while they discussed putting stove ash at the base of tomato plants to keep off cutworms or Mama bragged on how fast I was learning to read.

senses: A blue-veined Italian cheese, made from cow's milk.
ety: Borrowed from Italian Gorgonzola, a town in northern Italy where the cheese originated.

senses: A garment incorporating a niqab (veil for the face).
ety: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi बुरक़ा (burqā) / Urdu بُرْقَع (burqa')), from Classical Persian بُرْقَع (burqa'), from Arabic بُرْقُع (burquʕ).

senses: The practices, methods, aims, and spirit of commerce or business.
A tendency to value profit over everything else.
Not suitable or able to be filmed.
examples: The dense, bleak, multilayered graphic novel was declared unfilmable first by its writer Alan Moore and then by 12 Monkeys director Terry Gilliam, who was the first man to try and fail.
But Benioff, Weiss, and their collaborator Alexander Woo have undoubtedly proved yet again that there is no such thing as an unfilmable novel.

senses: Easy to drink.
examples: The southern wines are simpler and more quaffable, the reds often heady (Côtes du Rhône Villages Cairanne is a good example), the rosés lively and fresh (Tavel), and the whites fruity and smooth (Cairanne).

senses: A kind of merger by which one or more shareholders who collectively hold a majority of shares in a corporation gain ownership of remaining shares in that corporation.
A tournament in which players are gradually eliminated and the last remaining player wins everything gambled.
To show enthusiasm.
ety: First attested from 1827. Back-formation from enthusiasm, from Ancient Greek ἔνθεος (éntheos, “possessed by a god”), from ἐν (en, “in”) + θεός (theós, “god”)

senses: A counter or token.
examples: The girl took a jeton and was given a fresh towel which she draped over her arm like a waiter.

senses: An ancient Indian game, its rules not fully known, presumed to be the ancestor of chess and similar games.
A rope, strap, chain, or line used to secure a load or item.
The assembly to which something is secured using a tiedown.
The act of securing something using a tiedown.
examples: Accomplish aircraft tiedown by utilizing mooring points shown in figure 2-28.

senses: A martial art developed in Brazil, involving complex acrobatic maneuvers and flowing movements.
A practitioner of this martial art.
ety: From Brazilian Portuguese capoeira, of uncertain etymology.

senses: One who is noted for being very fast.
A person who speeds (drives fast).
A vehicle or other device used for racing.
examples: With Deebo Samuel as their top receiver, they need to give quarterback Jimmy Garoppolo another top target. So they chose Brandon Aiyuk, the speedster from Arizona State.

senses: A small motorized ferry or sampan that serves mostly remote islands.
The female equivalent of a hitman; a female assassin for hire.
ety: From hit + woman, based on earlier hitman.
examples: On the show, the person who does most of the critiquing is Ms. Southwick, the delightfully acerbic hitwoman who has become the character to watch.

senses: The domain or totality of blogs and websites associated with the men's rights movement, passport bro's, NoFap, MGTOW, PUA, the redpill movement and incels.
ety: From man + -o- + -sphere, after the pattern of blogosphere.

senses: To express sexual desire upon seeing a person that one finds sexually attractive.
ety: Imitative of the sound made, with the mouth initially partly closed and then opened wide.

senses: Eggplant; aubergine.
ety: From Surinamese Dutch boulanger, from French beringène, from Arabic بَاذِنْجَان (bāḏinjān), from Persian بادنجان (bâdenjân). Doublet of aubergine.
examples: For quotations using this term, see Citations:boulanger.

senses: A flannelette shirt.
examples: There is a general notion of how this stereotype dresses (flannos and ugg boots and mullet hairdos) and eats (pizza and Coke).

senses: One who digs for clams.
The past environment of an area during a given period of its history.
A plotline that is metaphorically left to "dangle" or "hang"; in other words, the plotline is forgotten, phased out and eventually dropped, and thus a resolution is never achieved.
A large earring that hangs down far.
A speedometer, particularly one in a race car or other automobile.
examples: You don′t need to change dashboards since the switches and instruments are suited to the V8, although the speedo and tachometer will require modification to adjust them to your V8′s gearing and cylinders.

One further advantage of the ‘J’ type overdrive units is that the speedo drive gear on the rear drive shaft of the gearbox can be changed, thereby adjusting the speedo-drive ratio to suit the TR′s 15in wheels.
The main instruments are in the centre of the dash, finished in silver (grey on the GP); consisting of a circular speedo with petrol and temperature gauges on either side.

senses: A person who sells tobacco, cigarettes, cigars, snuff and sundry items.
A tobacconist's shop.
A person who is addicted to smoking tobacco.
Any female nature spirit associated with water, forests, grottos, wind, etc.
A young girl, especially one who is attractive, beautiful or graceful.
ety: From Middle English nimphe, from Old English nymphē and Old French nimphe, both from Latin nympha (“nymph, bride”), from Ancient Greek νύμφη (númphē, “bride, young maiden”). Doublet of nympha.

senses: Through or across a vein.
A member of a parliament, congress or an elected national legislative body of another name.
A person well-versed in parliamentary procedure.
Very nearly linear.
A bar made with rolled oats, butter, golden syrup, and brown sugar, baked in a tray.
ety: From flap (“to toss sharply”) + jack (“generic object”). So called from the process of baking it by flipping and catching it in the griddle when done on one side.

senses: Inconsistent with established standards of good form or taste.
ety: From Middle English unsemli, probably a partial calque of Old Norse úsǽmiligr (“unseemly”); equivalent to un- + seemly. Cognate with Icelandic ósæmileg (“offensive”), Norwegian usømmelig (“unseemly”), Danish usømmelig (“unseemly”), German unziemlich.
examples: He was drunk and made some very unseemly comments.
Yet this I can say, I was very wary of giving them occasion, by any unseemly action, to make them averse to going on pilgrimage.
Secrets that few would like to scrutinise were bred and hidden in mountains of unseemly rags, masses of corrupted fat, and sepulchres of bones.

senses: A dress, a piece of clothing, which consists of a skirt and a cover for the upper body.
An outer garment worn by priests and other clericals; a habit.
A sailor's jersey.
An undress regimental coat.
ety: From Middle English frok, frokke, from Old French froc (“frock, a monk's gown or habit”), perhaps via Medieval Latin hrocus, roccus, rocus (“a coat”), from Frankish *hrokk (“skirt, dress, robe”), from Proto-Germanic *hrukkaz (“robe, jacket, skirt, tunic”), from Proto-Indo-European *kreḱ- (“to weave”). Cognate with Old High German hroch, roch (“skirt, dress, cowl”) – whence German Rock (“skirt, coat”) –, Saterland Frisian Rok (“skirt”), Dutch rok (“skirt, petticoat”), Old English rocc (“an overgarment, tunic, rochet”), Old Norse rokkr (“skirt, jacket”), whence Danish rok (“garment”).

senses: A kind of demon held to be harmful to humans.
ety: From Cantonese 魔怪 (mo1 gwaai3), 魔鬼 (mo1 gwai2).

senses: Fitted with a sash (window opener).
Having a sash (cloth decoration).
examples: Seeing sashed windows in town, he got them into his own house.
A skylight of moderate dimension was overhead and at each end of the oblong space were two sashed port-hole windows easily convertible back into embrasures for short carronades.

senses: A scientist specialising in spectroscopy.
A relatively flat and arid valley that is surrounded by mountains and that drains into a central basin.
examples: In three separate bolsons in West Texas, electrical-resistivity soundings and seismic-refraction profiles have been used . . . to estimate the alluvium thickness and ground-water quality.
The image of a colossal purse is helpful in envisioning a bolson in the landscape: an extensive, saucer-shaped basin, closed at the bottom and surrounded on all sides by mountain slopes.
